items.stem: A slicer on a dashboard filters one chart but leaves two others unchanged. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The slicer is not connected to the other charts via Report Connections
options.rationale: Correct: a slicer filters only the PivotTables/charts it is explicitly connected to.

options.text: Slicers can only ever control one visual
options.rationale: One slicer can control many connected visuals.

options.text: The workbook must be saved to SharePoint first
options.rationale: Connection is unrelated to where the file is stored.
PivotCharts are filterable, including by slicers.

items.explanation: Correct: a slicer filters only the PivotTables/charts it is explicitly connected to.

items.stem: Which TWO practices make an Excel dashboard refresh reliably? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Base the visuals on a flat Excel Table or data model
options.rationale: Correct: a tidy structured source lets PivotTables and charts refresh cleanly.

options.text: Use PivotCharts linked to the data rather than pasted static values
options.rationale: Correct: linked PivotCharts update automatically when data changes.

options.text: Type the latest totals into the chart labels each month

options.rationale: Naming has no bearing on refresh reliability.

items.explanation: Correct: a tidy structured source lets PivotTables and charts refresh cleanly.

items.stem: Why should a dashboard be built on a flat table rather than a formatted report layout?

options.text: PivotTables and charts need structured, table-based data to analyse
options.rationale: Correct: a flat table is the structured foundation PivotTables require.
Printing is unrelated to the structure requirement.
Slicers work with tables and PivotTables.
Formatting choices are not the issue.
